fetch.pageTitle: Nagasaki Atomic Bomb Museum | Visit | English | NAGASAKI PEACE
fetch.pagePublisher: Nagasaki City (official website of Nagasaki City)

citations.quote: At 11:02 a.m. on August 9, 1945, the explosion of an atomic bomb devastated Nagasaki.
citations.comment: Time and date match. Page says the bomb 'devastated' the city; it does not say 'over'. The museum 'keeps that memory alive and teaches young people about peace' is not stated as such: page says 'We also consider it our duty to ensure that the experience is not forgotten but passed on intact to future generations.' and discusses how to inform young people about the horror of war and the importance of peace. Quotes came through WebFetch's text extraction.

problems: Publisher on the page is Nagasaki City (city-run site), the row says Nagasaki Atomic Bomb Museum
'teaches young people about peace' is only implied (page discusses informing young people), not a plain statement
'exploded over Nagasaki' is not the page's wording
suggestedFix: Optional: set publisher to 'Nagasaki City' and soften the museum sentence to match 'passed on to future generations'.

citations.quote: Nuclear reactions here – where hydrogen is fused to form helium – power the Sun’s heat and light.
citations.comment: Core fusion claim and H/He composition notes supported. Page also calls the Sun 'a hot glowing ball of hydrogen and helium'. Page does not literally say 'nearest star' (it calls it 'our solar system's only star' and names Alpha Centauri as the nearest stellar neighbour); that is common knowledge and true but not stated here. Quote via WebFetch extraction.

problems: 'our nearest star' not stated on the page

citations.quote: Nitrogen dilutes oxygen and prevents rapid burning at the Earth's surface.
citations.comment: Page lists dry-air shares: nitrogen 78.084%, oxygen 20.946%, argon 0.934%, carbon dioxide 0.042%, so N most common, O, Ar and CO2 (C) all supported. The page does not mention atoms or molecules, so 'made of atoms and molecules' is not backed by it (general knowledge). Argon being a noble gas is not checked on the page. Quote via WebFetch extraction.

problems: Page does not say air is made of atoms and molecules
'Ar: a noble gas' not confirmed on page
Publisher on page is NOAA; row says NOAA National Weather Service (JetStream is an NWS site, so acceptable)

citations.where: safety card "Myth: exposure makes you radioactive"
citations.quote: being exposed to radiation does not make one radioactive, except in very specific circumstances.
citations.comment: Page hedges with 'except in very specific circumstances'; the card states it flatly. The extraction found nothing on x-rays not contaminating a person, nor on washing material off skin or clothes (not found, but extraction may be lossy).

citations.where: safety card "Myth: microwaves are nuclear radiation"
citations.quote: The type of radiation that actually has sufficient energy to remove electrons from atoms is called ionizing radiation.
citations.comment: Also 'Microwave radiation is non-ionizing radiation.' supported. Page lists radio and television waves among familiar radiation but was not seen calling radio waves non-ionizing; 'microwaves make electrons vibrate to make heat' and 'damage tissue and DNA' not seen.

citations.where: safety card "Myth: a plant can blow up like a bomb"
citations.quote: The material in a reactor is distributed in such a way that it does not release energy instantaneously.
